html:
SMTO-HTTP-0076 — The connection's security certificate settings are incomplete

GUID: 6b04a168-8d85-4108-8b5f-a9ada5d45245
Slug: http-certificate-configuration-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The security certificate settings for this connection are missing a piece or mix two different sources, so SMTO can't use them. Nothing was sent to the service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP Connection, and find TLS verification. If it is Custom ca, choose one CA source and fill in only its field: CA certificate PEM or CA file path. SMTO needs exactly one certificate that tells it which issuer to trust for this service.
  2. If Client certificate is not None, fill in both the certificate and its key, as pasted text (Certificate and key PEM) or as files on the Gateway computer (Files on Gateway). A client certificate can't be used without its matching key, and both must come from the same kind of source.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. The test confirms SMTO accepts the certificate settings and can reach the service with them.

What success looks like

  • The connection saves without this message and Test connection shows Reachable.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who runs the service for the correct certificate files, and send them the copied error details. Keep the client key private: don't paste it into the conversation, a screenshot or an error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HTTP profile normalization rejected the TLS settings: custom_ca mode has zero or two CA sources, a client certificate lacks its key, or path and literal client-certificate sources are mixed.

What this means

  • Custom CA configuration has zero or two CA sources, a client certificate lacks its paired key, or literal and path client-certificate sources are mixed. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Custom CA configuration has zero or two CA sources, a client certificate lacks its paired key, or literal and path client-certificate sources are mixed.

How to diagnose it

  • Check source presence and pairing without exposing certificate private keys.

How to fix it

  • In the profile's tls section, custom_ca mode needs exactly one of ca_certificate or ca_path; client_certificate with client_key, or client_cert_path with client_key_path, must be set as complete pairs, and paths and literal PEM values cannot be mixed (normalize_profile in gateway_core/http_profiles.py). Correct the saved profile or the http.connect tls arguments; keep private keys out of logs.
  • Choose exactly one CA source for custom CA mode and configure a client certificate/key pair using either paths or literal material. Keep private keys private.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One selected CA source and any complete client certificate/key pair pass profile validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
